rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthened the youths to bear leaving home and comfort and to proclaim truth before the tyrant; speaking truth to a ruler is the best jihad because the ruler exposes its speaker to mortal danger.
rows.anchor: قويناهم حتى اقتحموا مضايق الصبر على هجر الأهل والأوطان والنعيم والإخوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabt literally ties an animal with a tether; figuratively, God tying a heart means giving it patience and firmness against fear.
rows.anchor: ربطت الدابة شددتها برباط والمربط الخيل ومن المجاز ربط الله على قلبه أي : صبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax attaches إذ قاموا to ربطنا, and their standing means rising to display the religious creed.
rows.anchor: منصوب بربطنا والمراد بقيامهم انتصابهم لإظهار شعار الدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes their standing as standing fearlessly before Decianus; on this reading their later words beginning هؤلاء follow their departure from him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد قيامهم بين يدي دقيانوس الجبار من غير مبالاة به

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward binding keeps the youths from worldly adornments and turns them wholly toward God; after awakening they preferred divine nearness to worldly life.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا} يعني : لئلا يلتفتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is creator and owner of the world; an idol is a created part of it and cannot be worshipped. The youths will never worship another deity, directly or in partnership.
rows.anchor: رب العالم ومالكه وخالقه والصنم جزؤ من العالم فهو مخلوق لا يصلح للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling idols gods rather than lords explains why the text says إله and directly rebuts the opponents' terminology.
rows.anchor: معبودا آخر لا استقلالا ولا اشتراكا والعدول عن أن يقال ربا للتنصيص على رد المخالفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shطط means speech exceeding the proper limit, either as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun or as an intensive verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قولا ذا شطط أي : تجاوز عن الحد فهو نعت لمصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They separated from their people in belief and resolved to separate physically by fleeing for their religion.
rows.anchor: الاعتزال بالفارسية (جداشدن) أي : فارقتموهم في الاعتقاد وأردتم الاعتزال الجسماني

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: After Decianus challenged them and gave them respite, Yamlīkhā, their leader, spoke to them on the road as they fled.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (قبل أزين كذشت كه دقيانوس بعد از معارضه ايشان مهلت داد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about what they worship may be a relative or a verbal noun; the exception is connected if they were polytheists like Meccans, but disconnected if they worshipped only idols.
rows.anchor: عطف على الضمير المنصوب وما مصدرية أو موصولة أي : إذا اعتزلتموهم ومعبوديهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He treats take refuge in the cave as the answer to إذ, like saying: when you do something, then do this.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء هو جواب إذ كما تقول إذ فعلت فافعل كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave command may indicate the unstated answer: inward separation from the people entails bodily withdrawal, or those wishing to leave should take refuge there.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو دليل على جوابه أي : إذ اعتزلتموهم اعتزالا اعتقاديا فاعتزلوهم اعتزالا جسمانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ideological separation entails bodily withdrawal; Rasteghfanī consequently ruled out marriage between Sunnis and Muʿtazilites.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الاعتزال الاعتقادي يوجب الاعتزال الجسماني

rows.speaker: رستغفني
rows.claim: Asked about marriage between Sunnis and Muʿtazilites, he ruled it impermissible.
rows.anchor: سئل الرستغفني عن المناكحة بين أهل السنة وبين أهل الاعتزال فقال : لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands His favor in both worlds and makes their flight for religion easy and beneficial; their certainty and trust explain their confidence.
rows.anchor: يبسط لكم ويوسع عليكم {ربكم} مالك أمركم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith instructs people to call on God while certain of receiving an answer.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ادعوا الله وأنتم موقنون بالإجابة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse inwardly describes a sincere seeker leaving bad companions, worshipping God alone, turning from everything else, and relying on God as he flees to Him.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن التائب الصادق والطالب المحق من اعتزل عن قومه وترك أهل صحبته

rows.speaker: الحجندي
rows.claim: His verse teaches that union is attained only by severance, beginning with cutting oneself off from everything else.
rows.anchor: قال الحجندي : وصل ميسر نشود جز بقطع قطع نخست از همه ببريدنست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the quoted verse praises retreat as a pleasant state for someone who inhabits the corner of seclusion.
rows.anchor: خوش وقت آنكه معتكف كنج عزلتست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker should cling to a perfected guide who trains him, increases his guidance, and strengthens his heart through spiritual care.
rows.anchor: متمسكا بذيل إرادة شيخ كامل مكمل واصل موصل ليربيه ويزيد في هدايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Mathnawī couplet warns that walking without a guide breeds self-conceit, error, and humiliation, and urges following the shaykh to receive his aid.
rows.anchor: كره شيرى ون روى ره بى دليل خويش بيني در ضلالي وذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Cave youths were unusually drawn by God and raised without an intermediary; this is rare, while the normal way is guidance through prophets and then learned scholars and shaykhs.
rows.anchor: ولكنهم كانوا مجذوبين من الله مربوبين بربهم وذلك من النوادر ولا حكم للنادر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that God educated him and made his education excellent, illustrating direct divine instruction.
rows.anchor: وإليه يشير قوله عليه السلام : "إن الله أدبني فأحسن تأديبي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking refuge in the cave inwardly means retreating into solitude and holding to guides who lead along the Sufi path.
rows.anchor: ففي قوله : {فأووا إلى الكهف} إشارة إلى الالتجاء بالخلوة والتمسك بالمشايخ المسلكين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Special mercy means God's personal favor, drawing seekers into His attributes so they acquire their qualities; general mercy is shared by believers and unbelievers, jinn, humans, and animals.
rows.anchor: أي : ينشر لكم طريق الوصول والوصال كما في "التأويلات النجمية"

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The prepared benefit is an opened path to arrival and union with God.
rows.anchor: أي : ينشر لكم طريق الوصول والوصال كما في "التأويلات النجمية"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in ترى may be to Muhammad or anyone capable of seeing; it describes what one would see at the cave, not an event actually witnessed.
rows.anchor: يا محمد أو يا من يصلح للخطاب ويتأتى منه الرؤية وليس المراد به الإخبار بوقوع الرؤية تحقيقا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: His story says a shepherd led the youths into the cave, God caused them to sleep, Decianus later learned of their flight and sealed the entrance to kill them inside, while two believing courtiers recorded their names and story on a stone tablet for a future discoverer.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (آورده اندكه جوانان اتفاق نموده بكوه در آمدند وشبان ايشانرا بغار در آورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's turning and passing describes the time before Decianus sealed the cave, since sunlight could not enter a sealed entrance and need to be diverted.
rows.anchor: فيكون ما ذكر في الآية من تزاور الشمس وقرضها طالعة وغاربة قبل أن سد دقيانوس باب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazāwar means turning and inclining, with one of the two tāʾs omitted; the right side faces west for someone facing the cave's depth, and the south-facing cave or miraculous diversion keeps the sun from them.
rows.anchor: أي : تتزاور وتتنحى وتميل بحذف إحدى التاءين من الزور بفتح الواو وهو الميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At sunset the sun cuts past without approaching them; al-Qāmūs glosses this as passing by and leaving them on its left, the eastern side of the cave.
rows.anchor: القرض القطع ومنه المقراض أي : تقطعهم ولا تقربهم {ذات الشمال}

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon glosses the sun passing them on the left as leaving them to the north, passing by, cutting past, and leaving them on its left.
rows.anchor: وفي "القاموس" تقرضهم ذات الشمال أي : تخلفهم شمالا وتجاوزهم وتقطعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajwah means open space or broad courtyard; the circumstantial clause stresses the marvel that the sun avoids them all day although their spacious position is exposed to it.
rows.anchor: الفجوة الفرجة وما اتسع من الأرض وساحة الدار وهي جملة حالية مبنية لكون ذات أمرا بديعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's course is a wondrous sign of God's knowledge and power, the truth of monotheism, and His honoring those devoted to Him.
rows.anchor: ما صنع الله بهم من تزاور الشمس وقرضها حالتي الطلوع والغروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance statement either praises the youths as guided or teaches that signs benefit only those God enables to discern them; whoever chooses misguidance has no possible protecting guide.
rows.anchor: والمراد إما الثناء عليهم بأنهم المهتدون أو التنبيه على أن أمثال هذه الآية كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their open eyes made an observer suppose they were awake; yaqiz and raqid are broken plural forms like the forms for weeping and prostrating in Sūrat Maryam.
rows.anchor: تظنهم والخطاب فيه كما في ترى {أيقاظا} متنبهين جمع يقظ بفتح القاف وكسرها

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: The youths symbolize spiritual champions: outwardly active in works, inwardly absorbed in divine grace and free of worldly concerns, awake in appearance but inactive within.
rows.anchor: در كشف الأسرار آلأرده كه اين حال نموداركار جوانمردان طريقتست ون بظواهر ايشان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels turned them in sleep so the ground would not consume their bodies; ذات اليمين is an adverbial phrase for the side facing their right.
rows.anchor: في رقدتهم بأيدي الملائكة {ذات اليمين} نصب على الظرفية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: He reports that the youths were turned twice each year.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه : كانت لهم تقلبتان في السنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reports that they were turned once from side to side on Ashura so the earth would not consume their flesh.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما تقلبة واحدة من جانب إلى جانب لئلا تأكل الأرض لحومهم

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: He objects that God could preserve them without turning them; Saʿdī al-Muftī answers that God ordinarily makes things occur through causes.
rows.anchor: وتعجب منه الإمام وقال : إن الله قادر على حفظهم من غير تقليب

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters derive from the verse leaning right while pronouncing negation in the testimony of faith and left during affirmation.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : الميل إلى اليمين عند النفي حين التلفظ بكلمة الشهادة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The cited inward reading begins an analogy about the seeker trained directly by God, who must surrender like a corpse before a washer.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة لطيفة وهي أن المريد الذي يربيه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A continued couplet compares a seeker entering the master's company with a drop entering a shell and becoming a shining pearl.
rows.anchor: كه قطره تا صدف را درنيايد نكردد كوهر وروشن نتابد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog was a shepherd's dog who followed their faith and was named Qitmir; basit depicts a past scene in the present, and its participle can work generally.
rows.anchor: هو كلب راع قد تبعهم على دينهم واسمه قطمير {باسط ذراعيه} حكاية حال ماضية

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, Hishām, and Abū Jaʿfar permit the active participle to govern without restriction; a forearm runs from elbow to the tip of the middle finger.
rows.anchor: وعند الكسائي وهشام وأبي جعفر من البصريين يجوز إعماله مطلقا والذراع من المرفق

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-waṣīd means the cave's courtyard or threshold; al-Suddī says the cave has no door or threshold and means the dog's place corresponding to a house entrance.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" الوصيد الفناء والعتبة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: A report says ten animals enter Paradise, including the animals of Salih, Abraham, Ishmael, Moses, Jonah, Ezra, Solomon, Bilqis, the Cave youths, and Muhammad; all become rams.
rows.anchor: على ما قال مقاتل عشرة من الحيوانات تدخل الجنة ناقة صالح وعجل إبراهيم وكبش إسماعيل

rows.speaker: سعدي
rows.claim: His verse says the Cave dog joined good people and entered Paradise in a ram's form.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره

rows.speaker: الإمام الثعلبي
rows.claim: He transmits that sending blessings on Noah protects one from ticks and carrying the written words about the Cave dog protects one from harm by dogs.
rows.anchor: ودر تفسير امام ثعلبي مذكوراست كه هركه درشبانروز

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: He says the Cave dog was a lion, which can be called a dog, as in the report that a lion ate ʿUtba b. Abī Lahab after the Prophet prayed against him.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن جريج أنه قال : كان أسدا ويسمى الأسد كلبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dogs are domestic or Saluqi, named for a Yemeni city with long hunting dogs; al-Zamakhsharī compares badly behaved commoners with Saluqi dogs and notes canine habits.
rows.anchor: والكلب نوعان أهلي وسلوقي نسبة إلى سلوق وهي مدينة باليمن

rows.speaker: الإمام اليافعي
rows.claim: One of the dog's ten traits is that when it leaves a place it does not look back, a sign of the sorrowful.
rows.anchor: كذا في "روض الرياحين" للإمام اليافعي رحمه الله {لو اطلعت عليهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one saw the sleepers, one would flee; الاطلاع means looking over something by direct sight. Fleeing is a verbal noun for turning away, and رعب is fear filling the chest.
rows.anchor: أي : لو عاينتهم وشاهدتهم وأصل الاطلاع الإشراف على الشيء بالمعاينة والمشاهدة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: He says the youths were terrifying because their eyes were open, their hair and nails had grown, and they lay in a dark, frightening place.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (مراد آنست كه كسى را طاقت ديدن ايشان نيست بجهت آنكه شمهاى ايشان كشاده است

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Muʿāwiya wanted to inspect the cave, Ibn ʿAbbās said even someone better than him had been barred by the verse; Muʿāwiya nevertheless sent men, and a wind burned them or drove them out.
rows.anchor: وعن معاوية رضي الله عنه أنه غزا الروم فمر بالكهف فقال : لو كشف لنا عن هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's bar means no one can scrutinize them; Muʿāwiya thought the bar applied only before awakening and discovery, while Ibn ʿAbbās knew it applied in every age.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : لا شك أن عبارة الخطاب في لو اطلعت وما يليه لحضرة الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address speaks to the Messenger but signifies anyone in his community, including Muʿāwiya; inspecting extraordinary matters is not accessible to every observer.
rows.anchor: لا شك أن عبارة الخطاب في لو اطلعت وما يليه لحضرة الرسالة وإشارته لكل من يصلح له من أمته

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: His story says Decianus sealed the cave and later died; under the pious king Tindrous, whose people disputed bodily resurrection, God awakened the youths as proof.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون دقيانوس دذر غار برايشان استوار كرده باز كشت وبدار الملك باز آمدند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their long sleep, preservation from decay, and awakening demonstrate God's power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: كما أنمناهم تلك الإنامة الطويلة وحفظنا أجسادهم وثيابهم من البلى والتحلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God awakened them so they would question one another, setting in motion the wisdoms that follow.
rows.anchor: {بعثناهم} أي : أيقظناهم من النوم {ليتسآءلوا بينهم} أي : ليسأل بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioner was their chief, whose name appears as Miksalmina; Bahr al-ʿUlūm records the form Maksalmina.
rows.anchor: هو رئيسهم مكشليينا. وفي "بحر العلوم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They guessed one day or part of one because they entered in the morning and woke late in the day, seeing the sun still above the horizon; this was a reasonable estimate, not a lie.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنما قالواه لما أنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة وكان انتباههم آخر النهار

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: He says they entered in the morning and, seeing the sun near afternoon, guessed they had slept a day or part of one.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (ايشان بامداد بغار بر آمده بودند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi's account is more apt because sending someone with money required enough daylight for a round trip, unlike awakening just before sunset.
rows.anchor: هذا أولى مما قبله لأن قوله فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم يدل على بقاء ما يسع فيه الذهاب والإياب

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Seeing their hair and nails grown, they told one another they had slept only part of a day.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (س ون ناخنان خودرا باليده ومويهاى سررا دراز يافتند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They concede that only God knows the actual duration because it was immense and indeterminate to them, renewing the division into two groups.
rows.anchor: أي : أنتم لا تعلمون مدة لبثكم لأنها متطاولة ومقدارها مبهم وإنما يعلمها الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They leave an irresolvable debate and send Yamlīkhā with silver; the demonstrative suggests a companion handed him the money for their day's food.
rows.anchor: قالوه إعراضا عن التعمق في البحث لأنه ملتبس لا سبيل لهم إلى علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coin may be minted or unminted; taking provisions is compatible with trust, because reliance follows ordinary means, as the Mathnawī teaches.
rows.anchor: والورق الفضة مضروبة أو غير مضروبة ووصفها باسم الإشارة يشعر بأن القائل ناولها

rows.speaker: مولانا
rows.claim: His couplet says that one who trusts should work and cultivate before relying on the Almighty; trust is no excuse for idleness.
rows.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : كرتوكل ميكنى دركار كن كشت كن س تكيه بر جبار كن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city was Tarsus, formerly called Ephesus; al-Qāmūs describes it as fertile and formerly Armenian before its return to Muslim rule.
rows.anchor: والمدينة طرسوس وكان اسمها في الجاهلية افسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted noun in أيها is its inhabitants; أزكى means more lawful, wholesome, abundant, or inexpensive, and رزق is bodily sustenance.
rows.anchor: أي : أهلها على حذف المضاف كقوله : {وسال القرية} (يوسف : 82) {أزكى طعاما} أحل وأطيب

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: He says the city had people who concealed their faith, so the youths hoped to obtain meat slaughtered by believers.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در زمان ايشان در آن شهر كسان بودندكه ايمان خود مخفى مى داشتند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Let him act courteously to avoid being cheated or act discreetly so they are not recognized; an old count puts the Quran's midpoint at this word.
rows.anchor: وليتكلف اللطف في المعاملة كيلا يغبن أو في الاستخفاء لئلا يعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not letting anyone sense their presence means avoiding acts that could lead to discovery, even unintentionally; the second reading reinforces careful conduct.
rows.anchor: من أهل المدينة فإنه يستدعي شيوع أخباركم أي : لا يفعلن ما يؤدي إلى الشعور بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If townspeople find them, they will stone them to death or force them back into unbelief; عَادَ can mean become, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: {إن يظهروا عليكم} أي : يطلعوا عليكم ويظفروا بكم والضمير للأهل المقدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the youths formerly followed the townspeople's religion before believing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا أولا على دينهم فآمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that their faith was new: the text says they believed, not that they were believers; coerced return to the religion they hated would be settled adherence and might become real under Satan's influence.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا هو الصواب لقوله تعالى : {إنهم فتية ءامنوا بربهم}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: After 309 years near God, the youths needed no physical food, nourished by spiritual food as the Prophet was when his Lord fed and gave him drink; returning to the self made them seek food.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" : العجب كل العجب أنهم لما كانوا ثلاثمائة سنة وتسع سنين في مقام عندية الحق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that he spent nights with his Lord, who fed him and gave him drink.
rows.anchor: كان يواصل الأيام ويقول : "أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقيني"

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Seeking wholesome food hints at realized people who, having tasted union, seek divine beauty in beautiful things as spiritual nourishment when back in the realm of the self.
rows.anchor: ففي طلبهم أزكى طعاما إشارة إلى أرباب الوصول وأصحاب المشاهدة لما شاهدوا ذلك الجمال

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
rows.claim: He says the realized are treated gently while disciples are treated severely; hidden states of lovers can look like unbelief to beginners, and the heedless may condemn them without insight.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو عثمان المغربي قدس سره إرفاق العارفين باللطف وإرفاق المريدين بالعنف

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: His story says Yamlīkhā found the city transformed after roughly three centuries; an old coin bearing Decianus's name led to his arrest as a supposed treasure finder, and people mocked his claim that Decianus summoned him the day before.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يمليخاكه بعقل كامل موصوف بود وصيتها قبول نموده روى بشهر نهاد

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: The townspeople took him to the king; he explained his companions had sent him for food and led them to the cave, where the king and nobles read the tablet and found the youths looking fresh in new clothes.
rows.anchor: القصه اورانزديك ملك آوردند وصورت حال تقرير كرد ملك باجماعتي از مقربان واشراف بلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with their sleep and awakening, God exposed the youths to display His power and wisdom and strengthen their certainty.
rows.anchor: كما أنمناهم وبعثناهم من تلك النومة لما في ذلك من إظهار القدرة الباهرة والحكمة البالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtharna means making people discover them, from the image of stumbling upon something hidden; the cause is named for the knowledge it produces.
rows.anchor: وأصله أن الغافل عن شيء ينظر إليه إذا عثر به فيعرفه

rows.speaker: تهذيب المصادر
rows.claim: The lexicon glosses إعثار as bringing someone upon a thing and اطلاع as bringing someone to hidden knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال في "تهذيب المصادر" الإعثار (بررسانيدن كسى را بر يزى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Discovery convinced people who denied bodily resurrection that God's promise is true: He held the youths' souls while preserving their bodies for centuries, then returned the souls, as He will gather all bodies for judgment.
rows.anchor: أي : الذين اطلعناهم على حالهم وهم قوم تندروس الذين أنكروا البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God graciously guided the people through the sign of sleep, proving the truth in a way that served as a messenger's proof for receptive hearts.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا من لطف الله بالقوم وإرشاده إياهم بصورة النوم

rows.speaker: الإمام الثعلبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet wished to see the Cave youths; Gabriel said he would not see them in this world, so he sent Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿAlī, and Abū al-Dardāʾ to invite them to Islam. Solomon's swift mount carried them; the dog first barked then recognized them. The youths awoke, exchanged greetings, accepted Islam, conveyed greetings to Muhammad, and slept again; they will awaken to greet the Mahdī and die before resurrection.
rows.anchor: در تفسير امام ثعلبي مذكور است كه حضرت رسالت صلى الله عليه وسلم را آرزوى آن شدكه أصحاب كهف رابه بيند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes attach إذ يتنازعون to an omitted اذكر; the author prefers this because it fits the following فاء and separates the phrase from what precedes.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أصحاب التفسير : هو متعلق باذكر المقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputants were the people of Tindrous, debating what to do with the site after the youths died again and how to conceal access.
rows.anchor: أي : تدبير أمر أصحاب الكهف حين توفاهم الله ثانيا بالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group proposed a building over the cave entrance to protect the grave and said God knew the youths, so outsiders need not know their location.
rows.anchor: {فقالوا} أي : بعض أهل المدينة {ابنوا عليهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims and their king resolved to build a mosque at the cave entrance for prayer and seeking blessing at the youths' place.
rows.anchor: لنبنين على باب كهفهم مسجدا يصلي فيه المسلمون ويتبركون بمكانهم

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: He lists ranks of saints and says they attained them through truthful scrupulousness, pure intention, sound hearts, and mercy toward Muslims rather than abundant worship or outward adornment. They curse no one, harm or belittle those below them, envy no one above them, and are generous, gentle, and pleasant.
rows.anchor: وعن الخضر عليه السلام أنه قال : ثلاثمائة هم الأولياء وسبعون هم النجباء وأربعون هم أوتاد الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward allegory, the company represents the spirit, heart, innate and acquired intellect, sacred power, and the secret faculties in the body's cave; Decianus is the commanding ego.
rows.anchor: اشارتست بروح وقلب وعقل فطرى ومعيش وقوت قدسيه وسر وخفى كه تعلق بكهف بدن دارد ودقيانوس نفس أماره است

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches etiquette in future commitments; it followed the Jews' instructions to Quraysh to ask about the Spirit, the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn. Muhammad promised an answer the next day without saying إن شاء الله; revelation paused, and Quraysh said his Lord had abandoned him.
rows.anchor: نهي تأديب أي : لأجل شيء تعزم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A future commitment is permissible only while conditioned on God's will; inwardly, choices and deeds all depend on God's will. When the qualification is remembered, one should say إن شاء الله.
rows.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من النهي أي : لا تقولن ذلك في حال من الأحوال إلا حال ملابسته بمشيئته تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet said إن شاء الله when the revelation arrived after his lapse.
rows.anchor: كما روى أنه عليه السلام لما نزل قال : "إن شاء الله"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks God for a clearer sign than the Cave youths' story as proof of prophethood; God gave him even more evident signs in distant prophetic histories and future events to the end of time.
rows.anchor: لشيء أقرب وأظهر من نبأ أصحاب الكهف من الآيات والدلائل الدالة على نبوتي

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Since the Jews made the Cave story evidence for Muhammad's prophethood, God diminished its importance with this wording, as at the chapter's opening.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : لما جعل اليهود الحكاية عن أصحاب الكهف دالة على نبوته هون الله أمرها

rows.speaker: السمرقندي
rows.claim: Another reading says that when someone forgets a thing, he should remember God and ask to be guided to something else that is closer, better, and more beneficial.
rows.anchor: وقال السمرقندي في "بحر العلوم" : والظاهر

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: One may die before tomorrow or be obstructed while alive; without conditioning a promise on God's will, failure would be a lie, repugnant and unfitting for prophets.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام في تفسيره : والسبب في أنه لا بد من ذكر هذا القول هو أن الإنسان إذا قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū al-Layth transmits via Abū Hurayra that Solomon vowed to visit one hundred wives to have warriors, forgot to say إن شاء الله, and all but one-half of a childless birth failed; the Prophet said the vow would have succeeded had he said it.
rows.anchor: روي أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : قال سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people act as if they have independent will, God customarily brings about the opposite to show that only He has true will.
rows.anchor: من لم يعلق فعله بمشيئته تعالى فإن من سنته أن يجرى الأمر على خلاف مشيئته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says complete faith includes making an exception in all speech, inwardly as well as outwardly; a merely verbal exception is ineffective.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن من تمام إيمان العبد أن يستثني في كل حديثه"

rows.speaker: مولانا
rows.claim: His couplet says that omitting an exception hardens intention, and the soul—not just passing words—must join the exception.
rows.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : ترك استثناء مرادم قسوتيست نى همين كفتن كه عارض حالتيست

rows.speaker: روضة الخطيب
rows.claim: A humorous story tells of a man who refused to say إن شاء الله while going to buy a donkey, lost his money, and later described the loss with repeated exceptions.
rows.anchor: ومن لطائف "روضة الخطيب" أنه سئل رجل إلى أين؟ فقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He permitted a delayed exception based on this verse, while most jurists rejected that rule because it would unsettle confessions, divorce, emancipation, and reports about the future.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما جوز الاستثناء المنفصل بالآية المذكورة وعامة الفقهاء

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: The verse allows a delayed exception to retract and escape sin, but an exception changing a legal ruling must be connected to the original statement.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي في تأويل الآية : هذا في تدارك التبري والتخلص

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: At al-Manṣūr's court, Abū Ḥanīfa ruled an exception after a pause to an oath ineffective; Ibn Isḥāq appealed to Ibn ʿAbbās's view, but Abū Ḥanīfa explained its valid interpretation and warned that broad use could let people evade allegiance. Al-Manṣūr imprisoned Ibn Isḥāq.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : لا يعمل الاستثناء لأنه مقطوع وإنما ينفعه إذا كان متصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The years clarify the youths' counted time in the cave while alive and asleep. The phrase is apposition, not a specification; the latter parse would imply 600 years under al-Khalīl or 900 under the usual plural minimum.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان لثلاثمائة لا تمييز وإلا لكان أقل مدة لبثهم عند الخليل ستمائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the tanwīn reading of مائة, the genitive plural follows; on the possessive reading, a plural stands for a singular, as in أعمالا.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة مائة بالتنوين وأما على قراءة الإضافة فأقيم الجمع مقام المفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra nine years convert the People of the Book's solar reckoning to the Arabs' lunar reckoning, with three years' difference per century; the source gives the lengths of solar and lunar years.
rows.anchor: أي : تسع سنين وهو إشارة إلى أن ذلك الحساب على اعتقاد أهل الكتاب شمسي

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: He calculates 300 solar years as 309 lunar years plus two months and nine days.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وبتحقيق سيصدسال شمسي سيصدونه سال قمري ودوماه نوازده روز باشد)

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: If people dispute the duration, he says to answer that God knows the time spent, since knowledge of the hidden belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : إن الأمر في مدة لبثهم كما ذكرنا فإن نازعوك فيها فأجبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows what is hidden from earth's inhabitants; the exclamation describes how perfectly He sees every existent and hears every audible thing.
rows.anchor: خاصة {غيب السماوات والارض} أي : ما غاب

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: He parses the pronoun after أبصر and أسمع as the subject of an exclamatory verb, with extra bāʾ; the form is not a command, and the exclamation is figurative since astonishment is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ في تفسيره الضمير في بهمحله رفع لكونه فاعلا لفعل التعجب والباء زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's perception exceeds created perception: nothing blocks it, and fine, coarse, small, great, hidden, and manifest are equal to Him; sight precedes hearing because the subject is visible things.
rows.anchor: لا يحجبه شيء ولا يحول دونه حائل ولا يتفاوت بالنسبة إليه اللطيف والكثيف والصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God sees every existent and hears every audible thing, and it is through Him that people see and hear.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {أبصر به وأسمع} أي : هو البصير بكل موجود

rows.speaker: القيصري
rows.claim: He describes divine hearing as disclosure through knowledge of essential speech, seeing as knowing realities through witnessing, and speech as disclosure through will and power that brings the unseen into existence.
rows.anchor: قال القيصري رحمه الله سمعه تعالى عبارة عن تجليه بعلمه المتعلق بحقيقة الكلام الذاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants of heaven and earth have no independently governing ally; God gives no being a share in His eternal decree because of His majesty and self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: يتولى أمرهم وينصرهم استقلالا ومن الأولى متعلقة بولي على الحال والثانية للاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recite the revelation as worship and a means of nearness, act according to it, and learn its secrets; do not heed requests for another Qur'an or a change.
rows.anchor: أي : القرآن للتقرب إلى الله تعالى بتلاوته والعمل بموجبه والاطلاع على أسراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilāwa is Quran recitation that follows and adheres to it, as in study and regular litanies; qirāʾa more broadly means voicing letters.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين التلاوة والقراءة أن التلاوة قراءة القرآن متابعة كالدراسة والأوراد الموظفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can alter God's words; the general statement is qualified by the verse about replacing one revelation with another.
rows.anchor: لا قادر على تبديله وتغييره غيره تعالى كقوله : {وإذا بدلنآ ءاية مكان ءاية}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an and its rulings never change by addition or loss and are preserved in memory; people change across ages as knowledge and practice revert to ignorance and abandonment.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن القرآن لا يتبدل أبدا ولا يتغير بالزيادة والنقصان سرمدا وكذا أحكامه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: He found a stone promising benefit if turned over; its reverse said that someone who fails to practice known knowledge cannot seek what he does not know.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله : مررت بحجر مكتوب عليه قلبني أنفعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He condemns the innovating Ilhāmiyya, who abandon learning and the Qur'an as a supposed veil and substitute poems for the Qur'an of the spiritual path.
rows.anchor: ومن فرق المتصوفة المبتدعة قوم يسمون بالإلهامية يتركون طلب العلم والدرس

rows.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
rows.claim: His couplet contrasts a heart weary of hearing the Qur'an with falsehood weary of God's true speech.
rows.anchor: قال الكمال الخجندي : دل از شنيدن قرآن بكيردت همه وقت وباطلان ز كلام حقت ملولى يست

rows.speaker: إبراهيم الخواص
rows.claim: He names five remedies for the heart: reflective Quran reading, an empty stomach, night prayer, dawn supplication, and company with the righteous; indulgence in desire leaves spiritual illness without refuge.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم الخواص : جلاء القلب ودواؤه خمسة : قراءة القرآن بالتدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to restrain and steady oneself in the companions' company; morning and evening can mean constant supplication, or seeking success in the morning and pardon in the evening.
rows.anchor: احبسها وثبتها مصاحبة {مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغدواة والعشى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelieving chiefs demanded that Muhammad expel poor companions such as Suhayb, ʿAmmār, and Khabbāb, citing their smell and low status and promising mass conversion if he sat with elites; Noah's people made a similar complaint.
rows.anchor: نزلت حين طلب رؤساء الكفار طرد فقراء المسلمين من مجالسه عليه السلام كصهيب وعمار وخباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though expelling a few companions might seem a lesser harm than keeping the chiefs in disbelief, someone who refuses faith because of poor company is a hypocrite, so his demand deserves no regard.
rows.anchor: الإيمان حذرا من مجالسة الفقراء لم يكن إيمانه إيمانا بل يكون نفاقا قبيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the dignity of prophethood, expelling believers for an uncertain prospect would be grave wrongdoing; such exclusion belongs to worldly rulers, while religious leaders attend to inward states.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير شان النبوة عظيم فلو طردهم لأجل أمر غير مقطوع كان ذنبا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's Face means seeking His pleasure, not a worldly benefit; the metaphor connects approval to the face where approval and anger are manifest.
rows.anchor: أي : مريدين لرضاه لا شيء آخر من أعراض الدنيا فالوجه مجاز عن الرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not let your gaze pass beyond the poor companions; the eyes are the grammatical subject, while the command addresses their owner and warns against disdaining their worn clothing to seek the rich.
rows.anchor: لا يجاوزهم نظرك إلى غيرهم

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: He reads the verse as God's admonition to remain with those who stay at the divine presence morning and evening; those whose eyes never turn from God deserve that the Prophet never turn from them.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو النون رحمه الله خاطب الله نبيه عليه السلام وعاتبه

rows.speaker: زبدة التفاسير
rows.claim: It treats تريد as oriented to the future, not a judgment that the Prophet desired worldly adornment; he warned against worldly life and the rich. Al-Kashifi says he never desired it; the point is not to act that way.
rows.anchor: وفي "زبدة التفاسير" : تريد حال صرف للاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not obey those demanding the poor be removed; heedlessness prevents grasping realities, and God made the Quraysh chiefs heedless of remembrance.
rows.anchor: في تنحية الفقراء عن مجلسك {من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawāʾ first means what the self loves and came to denote blameworthy desire opposed to religious law; an act is attributed to a servant by capacity and to God by creation.
rows.anchor: مصدر هويه إذا أحبه واشتهاه

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon says farat can mean injustice, aggression, or an affair exceeding its limit; here the chiefs leave truth behind, like a horse ahead of the herd.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : الفرط بضمتين الظلم والاعتداء والأمر المجاوز فيه عن الحد

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Following desire leads to ruin; the chiefs' opposition arose from heedless hearts occupied with fleeting falsehood, while honor lies in pure hearts and inner character, not outward beauty.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : {وكان أمره} في متابعة الهوى هلاكا وخسرانا وفي الآية تنبيه على أن الباعث لهم

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: His couplet says spiritual ascetics would not buy the satin robe of someone devoid of virtue.
rows.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
قلندران حقيقت به نيم جو نخرند

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says God looks at hearts and deeds rather than forms and wealth; good hearts and acts bring acceptance regardless of appearance or riches.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم وأموالكم بل إلى قلوبكم وأعمالكم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says angels questioned Abraham's suitability as intimate friend amid his attachments; God tested him through Gabriel, who offered to buy his twelve gold-collared dogs and flock. Abraham repeatedly let him take more, then gave all freely, refusing to revoke the gift when Gabriel disclosed himself. God directed him to sell them and endow the proceeds, which funded the shrine's endowment.
rows.anchor: روى أن الله تعالى لما اتخذ إبراهيم خليلا قالت الملائكة : يا رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth comes from God rather than desire; now that revelation has removed excuses, people choose what leads to salvation or ruin.
rows.anchor: ما يكون {من ربكم} من جهة الله لا ما يقتضيه الهوى فإنه باطل

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The truth includes glad tidings, warnings, and guidance along paths of happiness and away from destruction.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وقل الحق من ربكم} في التبشير والإنذار وبيان السلوك

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The permission to believe or disbelieve is a threat, not neutral license: God will not expel sincere believers to appease elites after the truth is clear, and human faith neither benefits nor harms God.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : {فمن شآء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not need faith and does not approve unbelief because it harms people, even if He wills it for some; gratitude and faith are pleasing to Him.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : {إن تكفروا فإن الله غنى عنكم}

rows.speaker: السمرقندي
rows.claim: People who will to believe should direct their capacity and will toward acquiring faith; this shows human choice together with God's creation of acts, a middle position between determinism and free agency, and makes reward and punishment just.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : فمن شاء الإيمان فليصرف قدرته وإرادته إلى كسب الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared fire for everyone who wrongs himself by choosing unbelief over belief; its canopy already surrounds them, with the past tense expressing certainty, and سرادق means a tent-like enclosure.
rows.anchor: هيأنا {للظالمين} أي : لكل ظالم على نفسه بإرادة الكفر واختياره على الإيمان

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: A surādīq is the set of wall panels around a tent, without a roof; Abū Saʿīd transmits the Prophet's description of four dense walls, each a forty-year journey in distance.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" السرادق ما يدار حول الخيمة من شقق بلا سقف

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: He transmits the Prophet's description of the Fire's enclosure as four dense walls, each the distance of a forty-year journey.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد قال عليه السلام : "سرادق النار أربعة جدر كثف كل جدار مسيرة أربعين سنة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the damned plead for drink, they receive molten metal in place of water; the irony resembles giving a calamity in place of lovers' reproach.
rows.anchor: كالحديد المذاب وقيل غير ذلك والتفصيل في "القاموس"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith describes the drink as oil sediment, thick and black; when brought near, the face's skin falls away.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام "هو كعكر الزيت" أي : درديه في الغلظة والسواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يشوي means roasting the faces; the drink fails to relieve thirst and instead burns them severely.
rows.anchor: {يشوى} (بريان كند وبسوزد) {الوجوه} إذا قدم ليشرب من فرط حرارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مرتفقا means a place to recline or dwell; its root is propping an elbow under the cheek, though comfort cannot be meant in Hell.
rows.anchor: تمييز أي : متكأ ومنزلا وأصل الارتفاق نصب المرفق تحت الخد

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: He says elbow-resting can express either rest or bewildered sorrow; rest is impossible here but sorrow is possible, so he rejects the alleged wordplay.
rows.anchor: وقال سعدي المفتي الاتكاء على المرفق كما يكون للاستراحة يكون للتحير والتحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word means an abode metaphorically, not actual leaning or comfort, since the place is Hell.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير المتكأ يعني (تكيه كله) بالفارسية والاعتماد لا يراد حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should shun wrongdoing and persistent sin; if they fall, repent and occupy themselves with monotheism and remembrance, since the road to Hell is long and its punishment severe.
rows.anchor: فعلى المؤمن الاجتناب عن الظلم والمعاصي والإصرار عليهما على تقدير الذلة فالتدارك بالاستغفار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says the least-punished person in Hell wears two sandals of fire whose heat makes his brain boil.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن أدنى أهل النار عذابا ينعل بنعلين من نار يغلي دماغه

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: He recounts a laughing, crying child playing in dirt; his self restrained him from greeting while reason urged him to do so. The boy invoked the Prophet's practice, said their souls had known each other in the unseen realm, explained our origin and return to soil and his response to divine punishment and mercy, then urged reflection.
rows.anchor: روي عن مالك بن دينار أنه قال : مررت على صبي وهو يلعب بالتراب يضحك تارة ويبكي أخرى
